item: The rollup benchmark meets the start-time guards of the served build and declines instead of building; the persisted connection is closed when the open fails after the attach
refs: R278; R189; audit 0.5.0 follow-up; Q GET side-effect table 2026-10-27; PR pending
summary: GET /api/diagnostics/rollup-benchmark built the whole-corpus keyword rollup in memory, the #1310 build, with no verdict: no exclusive window, boot order, memory guard, stop hold, killed-build marker or affordability check, and beside a served build. run_rollup_benchmark now takes the build lock without waiting (a running build declines it with build-running, and the lock is released after a decline or an error) and asks rollup_serve.first_start_decline(), the dispatcher's own verdict loop factored out unchanged, inside rollup_serve.inmemory_view(), a per-thread view in which _persisted_serve_active() is False: three of the verdicts stand aside for a persisted store, and the benchmark always builds in memory, so it must be judged as that build. A refusal returns available false, declined true, the verdict's reason, source and detail, and builds nothing; it does not overwrite the serve's last_skip. STATED: the per-batch memory-guard poll inside the build is the serve's alone (its hook also writes the build progress record), so the benchmark is bounded at its start by the verdicts and in the build by the budget's DuckDB limit; the cross-site guard on the GET route itself is RC2's. Second fix in the same change (audit nit, a defect under R189): columnar.open_store attached the persisted connection and, if read_store_meta or ensure_store_meta raised afterwards, fell back to memory without closing it, leaving the handle on the file and its memory held; the except path now closes it (and the file unlink needs the handle gone on Windows). 9 tests in tests/test_rollup_benchmark_guard.py, 2 in tests/test_rollup_store_kind.py; red-without by mutation: guard skipped fails 8, the in-memory view dropped fails 1, the lock dropped fails 9, the close dropped fails 2. The existing shape tests stub the verdicts out because they read the runner's memory.
